steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: Descriptive writing creates a vivid picture in the reader's mind using sensory details, figurative language, and careful word choices. It focuses on capturing a moment, place, or person rather than telling a story. | Golden Rule: Don't just describe what you see. Include sounds, smells, textures, and even tastes to bring your writing to life. | Core Principle: Instead of telling the reader what to feel or think, show them through specific details that allow them to experience it themselves. | Structure Options: Wide to narrow: Establish setting, then zoom to specific details Narrow to wide: Start with detail, then pull back to reveal context Pan across: Move through space like a camera panning

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What is the difference between descriptive writing and narrative writing? | Name three techniques for creating "show, don't tell" writing. | Why is it important to include senses beyond just sight?

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Golden Rule, Core Principle, Structure Options, and one past-paper question.
